name: Shimei (a Levite who received the tenth lot in temple service (1 Chron 25))
title: Levitical temple singer with the tenth lot
summary: Shimei was a Levitical musician and singer who served in the temple during King David's time. He was one of the sons of Jeduthun and received the tenth lot when David organized the musical divisions of the temple service. His service was part of the organized worship that David prepared for Solomon's temple.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as temple singer
keyEvents.description: Shimei was appointed as one of the Levitical singers during David's organization of temple service, as a son of Jeduthun.

keyEvents.title: The Tenth Lot
keyEvents.description: Shimei received the tenth lot, which determined his division and duty rotation in the temple. His group consisted of twelve people, including his sons and brothers.

keyEvents.title: David's Organization of Temple Service
keyEvents.description: King David organized the Levites into 24 divisions for singing and music in the temple, where Shimei and his family were assigned their place.

keyEvents.title: Jeduthun's Sons in Service
keyEvents.description: Shimei was one of six sons of Jeduthun who all served under their father's leadership with the harp, to praise and sing praises to the Lord.

keyEvents.title: The Role of Music in Worship
keyEvents.description: Shimei was part of a large musical community of 288 trained singers who served the Lord with song and instruments in the sanctuary.
